title: Rates, speeds and the best buy
objectives: Compute a rate such as a unit price or a speed
Compare options by converting them to a common unit
Separate a fixed fee from a rate

screens.prose: Two packs of the same coffee. Pack A is 250 g for £3.75. Pack B is 400 g for £5.60.
screens.question: Which pack is better value?

options.why: You picked the cheaper pack. A costs less in total, but you also get less coffee.
Equal value needs the same price for each gram. Work out the price of 1 g in each pack.

hints.text: Compare the price of the same amount of coffee in each pack.
Find what 1 g costs in each pack.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the price of one gram, not the price of the pack.

explain.text: A costs £3.75 ÷ 250 = 1.5p a gram. B costs £5.60 ÷ 400 = 1.4p a gram, so B is better value. The line from (0, 0) to B is less steep.

screens.prose: The line shows the price of any amount of coffee at a fixed price per gram. Move the slider until the line passes through pack B.
screens.question: What does 100 g of coffee cost at pack B's rate?

hints.text: Read the slider when the line goes through B.
The line through B rises £0.014 for every gram.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find B's price per gram, then scale it to 100 g.

byKey.per-gram: That is the price of one gram. 100 g costs 100 times as much.
byKey.grams-per-pound: You divided grams by pounds: 71.4 g for each £1. That rate is upside down for this question.

explain.text: The line passes through B at £0.014 a gram, which is £5.60 ÷ 400. So 100 g costs £1.40. A costs £1.50 per 100 g, which confirms B.

screens.prose: A **rate** compares two different quantities, such as pounds per gram or miles per hour. A **unit price** is the price of one unit. A third pack, C, is 1 kg for £13.50.
screens.question: What is pack C's price per 100 g?

hints.text: How many lots of 100 g are in 1 kg?
1 kg is 1,000 g.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Convert 1 kg to grams first.

byKey.per-kilo: That is the price per kilogram. 1 kg holds ten lots of 100 g.
byKey.per-gram: That is the price of one gram. 100 g costs 100 times as much.

explain.text: 1 kg is 1,000 g, ten lots of 100 g. So C costs £13.50 ÷ 10 = £1.35 per 100 g. That beats B's £1.40 and A's £1.50.

screens.prose: Speed is a rate too: miles per hour. A train covers 150 miles in 2 hours 30 minutes.
screens.question: What is the train's average speed in miles per hour?

hints.text: Write the time in hours before you divide.
30 minutes is half an hour.
2 hours 30 minutes is 2.5 hours. Divide 150 by 2.5.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn the time into hours first.

byKey.decimal-time: You wrote 2 h 30 min as 2.3 hours. Thirty minutes is half an hour, so the time is 2.5 hours.
byKey.per-minute: You divided by 150 minutes, which gives miles per minute. Multiply by 60 for miles per hour.
byKey.whole-hours: You dropped the 30 minutes. The trip took 2.5 hours, not 2.

explain.text: 2 hours 30 minutes is 2.5 hours, so the speed is 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 mph. On the graph, speed is the steepness of the line from (0, 0).

screens.prose: Two offers on the same batteries. Offer X: 3 for £4.50. Offer Y: 5 for £7.00.
screens.question: How much cheaper per battery is the better offer?

hints.text: Find the price of one battery in each offer.
X is £1.50 each and Y is £1.40 each.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the unit prices, not the totals.

byKey.totals: You compared the totals, £7.00 and £4.50. They buy different numbers of batteries.
byKey.per-two: You compared X with Y over two batteries. The question asks per battery: £1.50 and £1.40.

explain.text: X costs £4.50 ÷ 3 = £1.50 a battery and Y costs £7.00 ÷ 5 = £1.40. Y is £0.10 cheaper for each battery. Its line from (0, 0) is less steep.

screens.prose: A 500 g jar of honey costs £4.40. A 1 kg jar costs £9.00. A shopper grabs the big jar, because buying in bulk is always cheaper.
screens.question: Which jar is better value?

options.why: You trusted that bulk is cheaper. Per 100 g the big jar costs 90p and the small jar 88p.
The big jar holds twice as much but costs more than twice as much: £9.00 against 2 × £4.40 = £8.80.

hints.text: What would two small jars cost?
Two small jars hold 1 kg, the same as the big jar.
2 × £4.40 = £8.80, which is less than £9.00.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put both jars on the same unit before you compare.

byKey.bulk: You trusted that bulk is cheaper. Two small jars give 1 kg for £8.80, 20p less than the big jar.

explain.text: Per 100 g the small jar costs £4.40 ÷ 5 = 88p and the big jar £9.00 ÷ 10 = 90p. Bulk is often cheaper, but not always. Only the unit price can tell you.

screens.prose: Every time, you divided to put the options on one unit. $$\text{unit price} = \frac{\text{total price}}{\text{quantity}}, \qquad \text{speed} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$$ On a graph, a rate is the steepness of the line from $(0, 0)$.
screens.question: On a graph of price against grams, which line from (0, 0) shows the best value?

options.why: Steeper means more pounds for each gram. That is the worst value.
The length shows how big the pack is and its total price, not the price per gram.

feedback.correct: Least steep means fewest pounds per gram.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Think about what the steepness of the line measures.

explain.text: Steepness is the price added for each extra gram: the unit price. The least steep line charges least per gram. That was pack C among the coffees.

screens.prose: Turn pack B's price, £5.60 for 400 g, into a price per gram in pence. Each line changes one thing.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: $\dfrac{5.60 \text{ pounds}}{400 \text{ g}}$, the rate as written
$= \dfrac{140\text{p}}{100 \text{ g}}$, dividing top and bottom by 4
$= 1.4\text{p}$ per gram, dividing top and bottom by 100

hints.text: Which line is the price exactly as given?
Change the units of money before you shrink the amount of coffee.
Pounds to pence, then 400 g down to 100 g, then down to 1 g.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from the rate as written.

byKey.hundred: That line uses 560p, so the conversion to pence must come first.
byKey.gram: Per gram is the last step, after 100 g.

explain.text: Dividing the top and bottom of a rate by the same number keeps its value. You went from £5.60 per 400 g to 1.4p per gram. Every line describes the same price.

screens.prose: A broker's note says you bought 240 shares for £1,849.20 in total. That includes a flat £6.00 dealing fee, charged once per trade.
screens.question: What price per share did you pay, before the fee?

hints.text: Does the fee depend on the number of shares?
Take the flat fee off the total first.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Remove the fee, then divide by the number of shares.

byKey.fee-in: You divided the whole bill, fee included. The £6.00 fee does not scale with the shares, so take it off first.
byKey.inverted: You divided shares by pounds, which gives shares per pound. The price is pounds per share.

explain.text: The fee is fixed, so it is not part of the rate. £1,849.20 − £6.00 = £1,843.20 buys 240 shares, so each costs £7.68. Including the fee would overstate the price at £7.705.

ideas: A rate divides one quantity by another of a different kind: pounds per gram, miles per hour.
To compare options, put them on the same unit first. Convert kilograms, minutes and pence before you divide.
On a graph a rate is the steepness of the line from the origin. A fixed fee is not part of it.

formula.name: Unit rate
formula.note: Take any fixed fee off the total first.

summary.trap: Bigger packs are not always cheaper per unit. Compare unit prices, never totals.

quiz.prose: Six cans cost £4.20. Ten cans of the same drink cost £6.50.
quiz.question: Which is better value?

options.why: You picked the lower total. Per can it is 70p, against 65p for the larger pack.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the price of one can.

explain.text: Six cans cost 70p each and ten cans cost 65p each. The ten-pack is better value by 5p a can.

quiz.prose: A cyclist rides 18 km in 45 minutes.
quiz.question: What is her average speed in km per hour?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write 45 minutes in hours first.

byKey.decimal: You wrote 45 minutes as 0.45 hours. It is three quarters of an hour, 0.75.
byKey.per-minute: That is km per minute. An hour has 60 minutes.

explain.text: 45 minutes is 0.75 hours. Her speed is 18 ÷ 0.75 = 24 km per hour. Check: in one hour she covers 18 + 6 = 24 km.

quiz.prose: You pay £3,762.00 for 450 units of a fund, with no fees.
quiz.question: What is the price per unit?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the total by the number of units.

byKey.inverted: You divided units by pounds, which gives units per pound.

quiz.prose: Data plan P gives 30 GB for £12.00 a month. Plan Q gives 50 GB for £19.50.
quiz.question: Which plan has the lower price per GB?

options.why: 40p is P's price per GB, and 39p is lower.

options.text: Plan P, because it costs less each month
options.why: You compared the monthly totals. Q gives 20 GB more for its extra £7.50.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide each price by its GB.

explain.text: P costs £12.00 ÷ 30 = 40p per GB. Q costs £19.50 ÷ 50 = 39p per GB. Q is cheaper per GB, though only by 1p.
